note: Every figure is an illustrative model built on public time-use data; see each claim's calculation and assumptions. NOT verified against live sources.

claims.claim: A U.S. life expectancy of about 77 years is roughly 4,000 weeks.
claims.source_title: Mortality in the United States (life expectancy at birth)
claims.publisher: CDC / National Center for Health Statistics
claims.population: U.S. adults / a full U.S. life expectancy
assumptions: Figure was authored from the agent's recollection of the cited dataset, NOT from a live lookup — verify against the source before this story is ever published.
Uses period life expectancy at birth, not a cohort projection.
claims.calculation: 77.5 years x 52.18 weeks/year = 4,044 weeks, rounded to 'about 4,000'.

claims.claim: About 26 years of a full life is spent asleep — roughly a third of it.
claims.source_title: American Time Use Survey (sleeping) and CDC sleep-duration guidance
claims.publisher: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics; CDC
claims.population: U.S. adults / a full U.S. life expectancy
assumptions: Figure was authored from the agent's recollection of the cited dataset, NOT from a live lookup — verify against the source before this story is ever published.
Averages a single daily figure across all ages, which smooths over large childhood/adult differences — illustrative, not a measurement.
claims.calculation: ~8.0 h/day averaged across a 77.5-year life (childhood sleep need is far higher than adult) = 226,300 h = 25.8 years ~ 26 years; 26/77.5 = 33% ~ 'a third'.

claims.claim: A normal working life is roughly 80,000 hours, about 9 years of round-the-clock time.
claims.source_title: American Time Use Survey (work and work-related activities)
claims.population: U.S. adults / a full U.S. life expectancy
assumptions: Figure was authored from the agent's recollection of the cited dataset, NOT from a live lookup — verify against the source before this story is ever published.
Assumes full-time continuous employment; part-time, caregiving gaps, and unemployment all change it materially.
claims.calculation: 40-year career x 250 workdays x 8 h = 80,000 h = 3,333 days = 9.1 years of 24-hour days.

claims.claim: Around 11 years of an adult life goes to screens; television alone averages about 3 hours a day.
claims.source_title: American Time Use Survey (leisure and sports: watching TV)
claims.population: U.S. adults / a full U.S. life expectancy
assumptions: Figure was authored from the agent's recollection of the cited dataset, NOT from a live lookup — verify against the source before this story is ever published.
The TV component is measured; the non-TV screen component is an estimate and is the weakest number in this story.
claims.calculation: ~2.8 h/day television across 60 adult years = 61,300 h = 7.0 years; adding non-TV leisure screen use brings the total to ~11 years.

claims.claim: A mean one-way commute of about 27 minutes adds up to roughly one full year of a working life.
claims.source_title: American Community Survey (travel time to work)
claims.population: U.S. adults / a full U.S. life expectancy
assumptions: Figure was authored from the agent's recollection of the cited dataset, NOT from a live lookup — verify against the source before this story is ever published.
Covers commuters only; remote and non-working years are excluded.
claims.calculation: 26.8 min each way x 2 = 53.6 min/day x 250 days x 40 years = 8,933 h = 372 days ~ 1 year.

claims.claim: About 4.5 years of an adult life goes to household upkeep.
claims.population: U.S. adults / a full U.S. life expectancy
assumptions: Figure was authored from the agent's recollection of the cited dataset, NOT from a live lookup — verify against the source before this story is ever published.
Household-activity time differs sharply by household composition.
claims.calculation: ~1.8 h/day x 365 x 60 adult years = 39,400 h = 4.5 years.

claims.claim: About 2.5 years of an adult life is spent eating and drinking.
claims.source_title: American Time Use Survey (eating and drinking)
claims.population: U.S. adults / a full U.S. life expectancy
assumptions: Figure was authored from the agent's recollection of the cited dataset, NOT from a live lookup — verify against the source before this story is ever published.
Excludes time spent preparing food, which sits in household activities above.
claims.calculation: ~1.0 h/day x 365 x 60 adult years = 21,900 h = 2.5 years.

claims.claim: After sleep, work, screens, travel, upkeep and eating, roughly 9 years of genuinely discretionary waking time remain.
claims.source_title: Derived from the American Time Use Survey categories above
claims.population: U.S. adults / a full U.S. life expectancy
assumptions: Figure was authored from the agent's recollection of the cited dataset, NOT from a live lookup — verify against the source before this story is ever published.
The childhood/late-life deduction is the softest assumption in the film and is deliberately generous, so the 9-year figure is a ceiling rather than a floor.
claims.calculation: 77.5 - 26 sleep - 9 work - 11 screens - 1 commute - 4.5 upkeep - 2.5 eating = 23.5 years, of which childhood and late-life dependency absorb roughly 14, leaving ~9 years of discretionary adult time.
